title: Performance Evaluation of FTTH WDM-PON Networks for Fog Computing Infrastructure in Urban Environments
content: The expansion of IoT and latency-sensitive applications has driven the adoption of Fog Computing, which pushes computational resources to the network edge. The performance of such infrastructures depends critically on the underlying optical access network. This study evaluates FTTH WDM-PON networks for interconnecting Fog nodes in urban environments by comparing star and tree topologies through OptiSystem simulations. Performance was assessed via Q-factor, BER, and eye diagrams under varying power (-7 to +5 dBm), distance (5 to 150 km), and bit rate (2.5 to 100 Gbit/s). The star topology consistently outperforms the tree topology, achieving Q-factor > 10 and BER < 10⁻²⁷ up to 50 km and 10 Gbit/s, while the tree topology degrades rapidly beyond 25 km. These results demonstrate that the star topology is the preferred choice for critical Fog applications requiring high bandwidth and reliability. We provide practical recommendations for network operators regarding topology selection and node positioning for FTTH-based Fog Computing deployments in urban areas.
